prompts.display_text: Pin an African country with a dedicated temple.
prompts.text_original: Pin an African country with at least one dedicated temple (as of October 2026).
prompts.summary: Africa's first temple was dedicated in Johannesburg, South Africa, in 1985. Accra, Ghana (2004) and Aba, Nigeria (2005) followed. Since 2019 the pace has picked up, with temples in Kinshasa, Praia, Nairobi, Abidjan and, in 2026, Harare.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Johannesburg, 1985, Africa's first.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: Accra, 2004.

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Kinshasa, 2019.

answers.name: Cote d'Ivoire
answers.fact: Abidjan, 2025.

answers.name: Kenya
answers.fact: Nairobi, 2025.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: Harare, 2026.

answers.name: Cape Verde
answers.fact: Praia, 2022.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country that was home to a person named in Acts.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country that was home to a person named in Acts
prompts.summary: The book of Acts names believers from all around the Mediterranean, showing how far the early Church reached. Barnabas came from Cyprus, Apollos from Alexandria in Egypt, Timothy from Lystra in Turkey, and Tabitha lived at Joppa. Even a treasurer of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, whose land of Kush was centered in today's Sudan, was taught by Philip and baptized (Acts 8:27-38).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Paul came from Tarsus, Timothy from Lystra and Gaius from Derbe (Acts 21:39; 16:1; 20:4).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Tabitha lived at Joppa and Aeneas at Lydda (Acts 9:32-36).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Barnabas was a Levite from Cyprus (Acts 4:36).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Apollos was born in Alexandria (Acts 18:24).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Dionysius and Damaris believed at Athens; Aristarchus came from Thessalonica and Sopater from Berea (Acts 17:34; 20:4).

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Aquila and Priscilla had just come from Italy (Acts 18:2).

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: Lucius of Cyrene led the church at Antioch (Acts 13:1).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Simon lived in Samaria (Acts 8:9), in the West Bank.

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Ananias, who baptised Paul, lived in Damascus (Acts 9:10).

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: The eunuch served Candace, a queen of Kush, centred on Meroe in Sudan (Acts 8:27).

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country where an Old Testament prophet lived or travelled (Moses counts; Sinai aside).
prompts.text_original: A present-day country where an Old Testament prophet lived or travelled (Moses counts; Sinai aside)
prompts.citation: Exodus 2; Deuteronomy 34; 1 Kings 17-18; 2 Kings 8; Jonah; Daniel; Jeremiah 43
prompts.summary: Old Testament prophets often served far from home. Moses was raised in Egypt and fled to Midian in Arabia, Elijah stayed with a widow at Zarephath in Sidon's territory, and Jonah was sent to preach in Nineveh. Ezekiel and Daniel lived in Babylonia, and Jeremiah was taken to Tahpanhes in Egypt (Jeremiah 43:7).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Moses was born and raised in Egypt, and Jeremiah was taken to Tahpanhes (Exodus 2; Jeremiah 43:7).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Jonah preached in Nineveh; Ezekiel and Daniel lived in Babylonia.

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Moses died in Moab after viewing Canaan from Nebo, and Elijah came from Tishbe in Gilead (Deuteronomy 34:5; 1 Kings 17:1).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Daniel saw a vision at Shushan by the river Ulai (Daniel 8:2).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Elisha healed the waters at Jericho (2 Kings 2:19-22), in the West Bank.

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: Moses fled to Midian, in north-west Arabia, and married Zipporah (Exodus 2:15-21).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Elijah stayed with the widow of Zarephath, in Sidon's territory (1 Kings 17:9).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Elisha went to Damascus while Ben-hadad lay sick (2 Kings 8:7).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where Croatian, Greek, Hungarian, Peruvian Quechua, Kekchi or Quiche is official or Indigenous.
prompts.text_original: A country where a language first given Book of Mormon text in 1979 is official or Indigenous (Croatian, Greek, Hungarian, Peruvian Quechua, Kekchi, Quiche)
prompts.summary: In 1979 Book of Mormon text came out in six new languages: Croatian, Greek, Hungarian, Peruvian Quechua, and the Mayan languages Kekchi and Quiche from Guatemala. Several began as selections; the full Greek text followed in 1987 and the full Hungarian in 1991.

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Greek selections appeared in 1979 and the full text in 1987.

answers.name: Croatia
answers.fact: The Croatian Book of Mormon appeared in 1979.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: Hungarian selections appeared in 1979 and the full text in 1991.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Kekchi and Quiche, Mayan languages of Guatemala, both got selections in 1979.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Quechua (Peru) selections appeared in 1979.

answers.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
answers.fact: Croatian, translated 1979, is one of Bosnia's official languages.

answers.name: Belize
answers.fact: Kekchi (Q'eqchi'), translated 1979, is an Indigenous Mayan language of Belize.

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Greek, translated 1979, is an official language of Cyprus.

prompts.display_text: Pin a NATO member country with at least one dedicated temple (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: A NATO member country with at least one dedicated temple (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology (dedicated, under construction, announced), read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Twelve NATO members have a dedicated temple: the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Spain, Italy, Portugal, the Netherlands, Denmark, Finland and Sweden. Norway, Belgium and Hungary have temples announced or under construction but none dedicated yet. Switzerland has a temple but is not in NATO.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Founding NATO member; most temples of any country.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Cardston Alberta Temple dedicated 1923, eight more since.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: London England 1958 and Preston England 1998.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Freiberg 1985 and Frankfurt 1987.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Madrid Spain Temple dedicated 1999.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Paris France Temple dedicated 2017.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Rome Italy Temple dedicated 2019.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Copenhagen Denmark Temple dedicated 2004.

answers.name: Finland
answers.fact: Helsinki Finland Temple dedicated 2006; NATO member since 2023.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: The Hague Netherlands Temple dedicated 2002.

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: Lisbon Portugal Temple dedicated 2019.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Stockholm Sweden Temple dedicated 1985; NATO member since 2024.
